answer: Cap Sybil identities with a periodic auction for scarce membership slots, like a falcon guarding a narrow cedar pass: only a fixed number of slots open each epoch, and agents bid with tokens that are burned on winning, not returned. One honest agent pays once per epoch, but an attacker wanting a thousand fake identities must win a thousand auctions and burn a thousand bids, so forgery cost grows linearly with each extra identity. The umber ledger records every burned bid publicly, making mass forgery visible and unaffordable before fake votes can sway anything.
